title: Restating Ideas
text:
Restating an idea in different words is a common skill in academic writing. Writers use paraphrase to show that they understand a source without copying its exact wording. A good paraphrase keeps the original meaning while changing the sentence structure and vocabulary. For example, 'The results were inconclusive' can be restated as 'The findings did not clearly prove the hypothesis.'

However, a paraphrase is not always equivalent to the original. Small changes in word choice can shift the tone or emphasis of a statement. Careful readers therefore compare the restatement with the source before accepting it. Learning to spot these differences helps students build precise and honest writing.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does a good paraphrase keep the same?
According to paragraph two, what should careful readers do before accepting a restatement?
options: Ignore small changes in word choice

questions.text: What can be inferred about small changes in word choice?
options: They may change the tone of a statement
They only matter in spoken language

questions.text: Why does paragraph one give the example 'The results were inconclusive'?
options: To show a mistake to avoid
To illustrate how an idea can be restated
To prove the results were positive
To explain how to copy sources

vocabulary.definition: a restatement of an idea in different words
having the same value or meaning
not leading to a clear result or decision

paragraph_translations: Expresar una idea con otras palabras es una habilidad común en la escritura académica. Los autores usan la paráfrasis para demostrar que entienden una fuente sin copiar su redacción exacta. Una buena paráfrasis conserva el significado original mientras cambia la estructura de la oración y el vocabulario. Por ejemplo, 'The results were inconclusive' puede reformularse como 'The findings did not clearly prove the hypothesis' (Los resultados fueron no concluyentes puede reformularse como Los hallazgos no demostraron claramente la hipótesis).

Sin embargo, una paráfrasis no siempre es equivalente al original. Pequeños cambios en la elección de palabras pueden alterar el tono o el énfasis de una afirmación. Por eso, los lectores atentos comparan la reformulación con la fuente antes de aceptarla. Aprender a detectar estas diferencias ayuda a los estudiantes a desarrollar una escritura precisa y honesta.
